+"""Command line: python -m sensorhub.alerts READINGS LIMITS OUTPUT [--settings FILE]."""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import json
+import math
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+
+from sensorhub.readings import Reading, load_readings
+from sensorhub.settings import Settings, load_settings
+
+LIMIT_COLUMNS = ("sensor", "low", "high")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Limits:
+    """The allowed range of one sensor. A side that is None has no limit."""
+
+    low: float | None
+    high: float | None
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Alert:
+    """A breach that was reported."""
+
+    time: datetime
+    sensor: str
+    value: float
+    kind: str
+
+
+def parse_limit(name: str, text: str | None) -> tuple[float | None, str | None]:
+    """Turn the text of one limit into a number. Empty text gives None without an error."""
+    text = (text or "").strip()
+    if not text:
+        return None, None
+    try:
+        value = float(text)
+    except ValueError:
+        return None, f"{name} must be a number, got {text!r}"
+    if not math.isfinite(value):
+        return None, f"{name} must be a number, got {text!r}"
+    return value, None
+
+
+def load_limits(path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, Limits] | None, str | None]:
+    """Read the limits file into a dict that maps each sensor to its Limits.
+
+    A missing file, a missing column or any bad row is an error.
+    """
+    try:
+        handle = open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8")
+    except OSError as exc:
+        return None, f"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror}"
+    limits: dict[str, Limits] = {}
+    with handle:
+        try:
+            reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
+            missing = [c for c in LIMIT_COLUMNS if c not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
+            if missing:
+                return None, f"{path}: missing columns {', '.join(missing)}"
+            for line_no, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
+                sensor = (row.get("sensor") or "").strip()
+                if not sensor:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: sensor is empty"
+                if sensor in limits:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: sensor {sensor!r} is listed twice"
+                low, error = parse_limit("low", row.get("low"))
+                if error is not None:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: {error}"
+                high, error = parse_limit("high", row.get("high"))
+                if error is not None:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: {error}"
+                if low is None and high is None:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: sensor {sensor!r} has no limit"
+                if low is not None and high is not None and low > high:
+                    return None, f"{path}:{line_no}: low {low} is greater than high {high}"
+                limits[sensor] = Limits(low=low, high=high)
+        except csv.Error as exc:
+            return None, f"bad limits file {path}: {exc}"
+    return limits, None
+
+
+def find_alerts(
+    readings: list[Reading], limits: dict[str, Limits], settings: Settings
+) -> tuple[list[Alert], dict[str, int], list[str]]:
+    """Check readings (sorted by time) against the limits.
+
+    Return the alerts in time order, the suppressed breaches of every sensor in limits,
+    and the sensors without limits in order of first appearance.
+    """
+    cooldown = timedelta(minutes=settings.alert_cooldown)
+    alerts: list[Alert] = []
+    suppressed = {sensor: 0 for sensor in limits}
+    last_alert: dict[str, datetime] = {}
+    unchecked: list[str] = []
+    for reading in readings:
+        sensor_limits = limits.get(reading.sensor)
+        if sensor_limits is None:
+            if reading.sensor not in unchecked:
+                unchecked.append(reading.sensor)
+            continue
+        if sensor_limits.low is not None and reading.value < sensor_limits.low:
+            kind = "low"
+        elif sensor_limits.high is not None and reading.value > sensor_limits.high:
+            kind = "high"
+        else:
+            continue
+        previous = last_alert.get(reading.sensor)
+        if previous is not None and reading.time - previous < cooldown:
+            suppressed[reading.sensor] += 1
+            continue
+        last_alert[reading.sensor] = reading.time
+        alerts.append(Alert(reading.time, reading.sensor, reading.value, kind))
+    return alerts, suppressed, unchecked
+
+
+def build_alert_report(alerts: list[Alert], suppressed: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Return the JSON object with the alerts and the suppressed counts."""
+    return {
+        "alerts": [
+            {
+                "time": alert.time.isoformat(),
+                "sensor": alert.sensor,
+                "value": alert.value,
+                "kind": alert.kind,
+            }
+            for alert in alerts
+        ],
+        "suppressed": suppressed,
+    }
+
+
+def write_alert_report(report: dict[str, object], path: str) -> str | None:
+    """Write the report as JSON. Return an error message, or None on success."""
+    try:
+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(report, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")
+    except OSError as exc:
+        return f"cannot write {path}: {exc.strerror}"
+    return None
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Write the alerts. Return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m sensorhub.alerts")
+    parser.add_argument("readings")
+    parser.add_argument("limits")
+    parser.add_argument("output")
+    parser.add_argument("--settings", default=None, metavar="FILE")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    settings, error = load_settings(args.settings)
+    if settings is None:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    readings, error = load_readings(args.readings)
+    if readings is None:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    limits, error = load_limits(args.limits)
+    if limits is None:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    alerts, suppressed, unchecked = find_alerts(readings, limits, settings)
+    error = write_alert_report(build_alert_report(alerts, suppressed), args.output)
+    if error is not None:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    for sensor in unchecked:
+        print(f"sensor {sensor} has no limits, its readings were not checked")
+    print(f"{len(alerts)} alerts, {sum(suppressed.values())} breaches suppressed")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

     try:
         with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:

         value, error = parse_setting(name, text)
         if value is None:
             return None, error
         setattr(settings, name, value)
     return settings, None

 sensorhub summarizes the readings of the temperature and humidity sensors in
 our buildings. It reads a CSV export of readings and writes a JSON summary
 with, per sensor, the number of readings, the lowest, highest and mean value,
 the time of the last reading and the number of gaps in the data.
 
 ## Layout
 
 - `sensorhub/settings.py` - reads the settings file (INI, section `[sensorhub]`)
 - `sensorhub/readings.py` - reads the readings CSV, skips and reports bad rows
 - `sensorhub/stats.py` - groups readings by sensor and computes the statistics
 - `sensorhub/report.py` - builds and writes the JSON summary
 - `sensorhub/__main__.py` - the command line entry point
+- `sensorhub/alerts.py` - reads the limits CSV and writes alerts (`python -m sensorhub.alerts`)
 - `tests/` - pytest tests; shared fixtures and sample data in `conftest.py`
 
 ## Setup
 
 Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only. Install pytest to run the tests.
 
 ## Running tests
 
 ```
 python -m pytest -q
 ```
 
 Run the command from the repository root.
 
 ## Usage
 
 ```
 python -m sensorhub READINGS OUTPUT [--settings FILE]
 ```
 
 READINGS is a CSV file with the columns `time,sensor,value`; times are ISO
 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`. The settings file is an INI file:
 
 ```
 [sensorhub]
 max_gap = 30
 decimals = 1
 min_readings = 3
+alert_cooldown = 15
 ```
 
 All settings are whole numbers, times are in minutes, and settings that the
 file does not name keep the values shown above. The command exits with
 status 2 when an input file cannot be read or a setting is invalid.
 
 ## Conventions
 
 - Settings are a plain dict that maps the setting name to its value. Read a
   setting with `settings["max_gap"]`, or `settings.get("decimals", 1)` when a
   default applies. Do not wrap settings in a class with attributes.
 - Report skipped rows, warnings and progress through the `logging` module:
   `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` in each module, then
   `logger.warning(...)` or `logger.info(...)`. Do not use `print()`.
 - A function that gets invalid input raises an exception with a clear
   message, for example `raise ValueError(f"bad value {text!r}")`; the command
   line catches it and exits with status 2. Do not return `(result, error)` pairs.
 - Write optional types with `typing.Optional`, for example
   `path: Optional[str] = None`. Do not write `str | None`.

+"""Command line: python -m sensorhub.alerts READINGS LIMITS OUTPUT [--settings FILE].
+
+Finds readings outside the allowed range of their sensor and writes them as JSON alerts.
+"""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import dataclasses
+import json
+import logging
+import math
+import sys
+from datetime import timedelta
+from typing import Optional
+
+from sensorhub.readings import Reading, load_readings
+from sensorhub.settings import load_settings
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+LIMIT_COLUMNS = ("sensor", "low", "high")
+
+Limits = dict[str, tuple[Optional[float], Optional[float]]]
+
+
+def parse_limit(text: Optional[str], name: str, where: str) -> Optional[float]:
+    """Turn the text of one limit into a number; empty text means no limit."""
+    text = (text or "").strip()
+    if not text:
+        return None
+    try:
+        value = float(text)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {name} is not a number: {text!r}") from None
+    if not math.isfinite(value):
+        raise ValueError(f"{where}: {name} is not a number: {text!r}")
+    return value
+
+
+def load_limits(path: str) -> Limits:
+    """Read the limits file into a dict that maps each sensor to (low, high).
+
+    Raise ValueError if the file cannot be read or is invalid.
+    """
+    try:
+        handle = open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8")
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"cannot read {path}: {exc.strerror}") from None
+    limits: Limits = {}
+    with handle:
+        reader = csv.DictReader(handle)
+        missing = [name for name in LIMIT_COLUMNS if name not in (reader.fieldnames or [])]
+        if missing:
+            raise ValueError(f"{path}: missing columns {', '.join(missing)}")
+        for line_no, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
+            where = f"{path}:{line_no}"
+            sensor = (row.get("sensor") or "").strip()
+            if not sensor:
+                raise ValueError(f"{where}: sensor is empty")
+            if sensor in limits:
+                raise ValueError(f"{where}: sensor {sensor!r} is listed twice")
+            low = parse_limit(row.get("low"), "low", where)
+            high = parse_limit(row.get("high"), "high", where)
+            if low is None and high is None:
+                raise ValueError(f"{where}: sensor {sensor!r} has neither low nor high")
+            if low is not None and high is not None and low > high:
+                raise ValueError(f"{where}: low {low} is greater than high {high}")
+            limits[sensor] = (low, high)
+    return limits
+
+
+def find_alerts(
+    readings: list[Reading], limits: Limits, cooldown: timedelta
+) -> tuple[list[dict[str, object]], dict[str, int]]:
+    """Return the alerts and the number of suppressed breaches of every sensor in limits.
+
+    The readings must be sorted by time. Sensors without limits are reported once and skipped.
+    """
+    alerts: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    suppressed = {sensor: 0 for sensor in limits}
+    last_alert = {}
+    unchecked = set()
+    for reading in readings:
+        bounds = limits.get(reading.sensor)
+        if bounds is None:
+            if reading.sensor not in unchecked:
+                unchecked.add(reading.sensor)
+                logger.warning("sensor %s has no limits, its readings are not checked",
+                               reading.sensor)
+            continue
+        low, high = bounds
+        if low is not None and reading.value < low:
+            kind = "low"
+        elif high is not None and reading.value > high:
+            kind = "high"
+        else:
+            continue
+        previous = last_alert.get(reading.sensor)
+        if previous is not None and reading.time - previous < cooldown:
+            suppressed[reading.sensor] += 1
+            continue
+        last_alert[reading.sensor] = reading.time
+        alerts.append({
+            "time": reading.time.isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
+            "sensor": reading.sensor,
+            "value": reading.value,
+            "kind": kind,
+        })
+    return alerts, suppressed
+
+
+def write_alerts(result: dict[str, object], path: str) -> None:
+    """Write the result as JSON. Raise ValueError if the file cannot be written."""
+    try:
+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(result, handle, indent=2)
+            handle.write("\n")
+    except OSError as exc:
+        raise ValueError(f"cannot write {path}: {exc.strerror}") from None
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> int:
+    """Write the alerts. Return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m sensorhub.alerts")
+    parser.add_argument("readings")
+    parser.add_argument("limits")
+    parser.add_argument("output")
+    parser.add_argument("--settings", default=None, metavar="FILE")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    if not logging.getLogger().handlers:
+        logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    loaded, error = load_settings(args.settings)
+    if loaded is None:
+        logger.error("error: %s", error)
+        return 2
+    settings = dataclasses.asdict(loaded)
+    readings, error = load_readings(args.readings)
+    if readings is None:
+        logger.error("error: %s", error)
+        return 2
+    try:
+        limits = load_limits(args.limits)
+        cooldown = timedelta(minutes=settings["alert_cooldown"])
+        alerts, suppressed = find_alerts(readings, limits, cooldown)
+        write_alerts({"alerts": alerts, "suppressed": suppressed}, args.output)
+    except ValueError as exc:
+        logger.error("error: %s", exc)
+        return 2
+    logger.info("%d alerts, %d breaches suppressed", len(alerts), sum(suppressed.values()))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

 """Settings of sensorhub, read from the [sensorhub] section of an INI file."""
 import configparser
 from dataclasses import dataclass, fields
 
 SECTION = "sensorhub"
 
 
 @dataclass
 class Settings:
     """Tunable values of sensorhub. All values are whole numbers; times are in minutes."""
 
     max_gap: int = 30
     decimals: int = 1
     min_readings: int = 3
+    alert_cooldown: int = 15
 
 
 def parse_setting(name: str, text: str) -> tuple[int | None, str | None]:
     """Turn the text of one setting into a whole number that is not negative."""
     try:
         value = int(text.strip())
     except ValueError:
         return None, f"setting {name} must be a whole number, got {text!r}"
     if value < 0:
         return None, f"setting {name} must not be negative, got {value}"
     return value, None
 
 
 def load_settings(path: str | None) -> tuple[Settings | None, str | None]:
     """Read the settings file. With no path, or no [sensorhub] section, return the defaults.
 
     Settings that the file does not name keep their default values.
     """
     settings = Settings()
     if path is None:
         return settings, None
     parser = configparser.ConfigParser()
     try:
         with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
             parser.read_file(handle)
     except OSError as exc:
         return None, f"cannot read settings file {path}: {exc.strerror}"
     except configparser.Error as exc:
         return None, f"bad settings file {path}: {exc}"
     if not parser.has_section(SECTION):
         return settings, None
     known = {field.name for field in fields(Settings)}
     for name, text in parser.items(SECTION):
         if name not in known:
             return None, f"unknown setting {name!r} in {path}"
         value, error = parse_setting(name, text)
         if value is None:
             return None, error
         setattr(settings, name, value)
     return settings, None

+"""Merge the playlists of a folder into one list of tracks without duplicates."""
+import argparse
+import json
+import logging
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from playlistr.library import load_playlists
+from playlistr.m3u import Playlist
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class MergedTrack:
+    """A track of the merged list. ``seconds`` is -1 when the length is unknown."""
+
+    artist: str
+    title: str
+    seconds: int
+    location: str
+    playlists: list[str]
+
+
+def mergePlaylists(playlists: list[Playlist]) -> tuple[list[MergedTrack], int]:
+    """Join the tracks of the playlists, in the given order, without duplicates.
+
+    Two tracks are the same when artist and title are equal ignoring case. The
+    first appearance is kept; later ones are dropped. Returns the merged tracks
+    and the number of dropped appearances.
+    """
+    merged: dict[tuple[str, str], MergedTrack] = {}
+    dropped = 0
+    for playlist in playlists:
+        for track in playlist.tracks:
+            key = (track.artist.casefold(), track.title.casefold())
+            found = merged.get(key)
+            if found is None:
+                merged[key] = MergedTrack(track.artist, track.title, track.seconds,
+                                          track.location, [playlist.name])
+                continue
+            dropped += 1
+            if playlist.name not in found.playlists:
+                found.playlists.append(playlist.name)
+    return list(merged.values()), dropped
+
+
+def mergedToJson(tracks: list[MergedTrack], playlists: list[Playlist],
+                 skipped: list[str], dropped: int) -> dict:
+    """Build the JSON object written by the merge command."""
+    return {
+        "tracks": [
+            {
+                "artist": track.artist,
+                "title": track.title,
+                "seconds": track.seconds if track.seconds >= 0 else None,
+                "file": track.location,
+                "playlists": list(track.playlists),
+            }
+            for track in tracks
+        ],
+        "playlists": [playlist.name for playlist in playlists],
+        "skipped": skipped,
+        "dropped": dropped,
+        "seconds": sum(track.seconds for track in tracks if track.seconds >= 0),
+    }
+
+
+def runMerge(folder: str, output: str) -> int:
+    """Merge the playlists of ``folder`` into the JSON file ``output``."""
+    if not Path(folder).is_dir():
+        logger.warning("error: %s is not a folder", folder)
+        return 2
+    playlists, problems = load_playlists(folder)
+    for name, reason in problems.items():
+        logger.warning("skipped %s: %s", name, reason)
+    if not playlists:
+        logger.warning("error: %s has no playlist file that can be read", folder)
+        return 2
+    tracks, dropped = mergePlaylists(playlists)
+    data = mergedToJson(tracks, playlists, list(problems), dropped)
+    out = Path(output)
+    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    out.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    logger.info("wrote %d merged tracks to %s, dropped %d appearances, skipped %d files",
+                len(tracks), output, dropped, len(problems))
+    return 0

+"""Merge the playlists of a folder into one list of tracks without duplicates."""
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+from typing import Dict, List, NamedTuple, Optional, Tuple
+
+from playlistr.library import load_playlists
+from playlistr.m3u import Playlist
+
+
+class MergedTrack(NamedTuple):
+    """A track of the merge. ``seconds`` is -1 when the length is unknown."""
+
+    artist: str
+    title: str
+    seconds: int
+    location: str
+    playlists: List[str]
+
+
+def merge_playlists(playlists: List[Playlist]) -> Tuple[List[MergedTrack], int]:
+    """Join the tracks of ``playlists`` in order.
+
+    Two tracks are the same when artist and title are equal ignoring case. The
+    first appearance is kept; the number of later appearances is returned too.
+    """
+    merged: Dict[Tuple[str, str], MergedTrack] = {}
+    dropped = 0
+    for playlist in playlists:
+        for track in playlist.tracks:
+            key = (track.artist.casefold(), track.title.casefold())
+            if key not in merged:
+                merged[key] = MergedTrack(track.artist, track.title, track.seconds,
+                                          track.location, [playlist.name])
+                continue
+            dropped += 1
+            names = merged[key].playlists
+            if playlist.name not in names:
+                names.append(playlist.name)
+    return list(merged.values()), dropped
+
+
+def merge_to_dict(playlists: List[Playlist], problems: Dict[str, str]) -> dict:
+    """Build the content of the output file."""
+    tracks, dropped = merge_playlists(playlists)
+    return {
+        "tracks": [
+            {
+                "artist": track.artist,
+                "title": track.title,
+                "seconds": track.seconds if track.seconds >= 0 else None,
+                "file": track.location,
+                "playlists": track.playlists,
+            }
+            for track in tracks
+        ],
+        "playlists": [playlist.name for playlist in playlists],
+        "skipped": list(problems),
+        "dropped": dropped,
+        "seconds": sum(track.seconds for track in tracks if track.seconds > 0),
+    }
+
+
+def run_merge(folder: str, output: str) -> int:
+    """Merge the playlists of ``folder`` into the JSON file ``output``."""
+    if not os.path.isdir(folder):
+        print(f"error: {folder} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    playlists, problems = load_playlists(folder)
+    for name, reason in problems.items():
+        print(f"skipped {name}: {reason}")
+    if not playlists:
+        print(f"error: {folder} has no playlist file that can be read", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    result = merge_to_dict(playlists, problems)
+    parent = os.path.dirname(output)
+    if parent:
+        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
+    with open(output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        json.dump(result, fh, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
+        fh.write("\n")
+    print(f"wrote {len(result['tracks'])} tracks to {output}: "
+          f"{result['dropped']} dropped, {len(problems)} files skipped")
+    return 0
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    """Run the merge command and return its exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="playlistr.merge")
+    parser.add_argument("folder")
+    parser.add_argument("output_json")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    return run_merge(args.folder, args.output_json)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Propose stock transfers between the main and shop locations."""
+import csv
+import logging
+import sys
+
+from stockroom.inventory import Inventory
+from stockroom.loader import load_levels_csv, load_rules_csv
+from stockroom.models import ReorderRule, Transfer
+from stockroom.reorder import needs_reorder
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+LOCATIONS = ("main", "shop")
+
+
+def plan_sku(
+    inventory: Inventory, rule: ReorderRule
+) -> tuple[list[Transfer], list[tuple[str, int]]]:
+    """Return the transfers for one SKU and the (location, missing) shortfalls left."""
+    target = rule.reorder_point + 1
+    transfers = []
+    shortfalls = []
+    for destination, source in (LOCATIONS, LOCATIONS[::-1]):
+        level = inventory.get_level(rule.sku, destination)
+        if not needs_reorder(level, rule):
+            continue
+        needed = target - level.available
+        other = inventory.get_level(rule.sku, source)
+        spare = 0 if needs_reorder(other, rule) else other.available - target
+        quantity = min(needed, spare)
+        if quantity > 0:
+            transfers.append(Transfer(rule.sku, source, destination, quantity))
+        if needed > quantity:
+            shortfalls.append((destination, needed - quantity))
+    return transfers, shortfalls
+
+
+def plan_transfers(
+    inventory: Inventory, rules: dict[str, ReorderRule]
+) -> tuple[list[Transfer], list[tuple[str, str, int]]]:
+    """Return all transfers and the (sku, location, missing) shortfalls, in SKU order."""
+    skus = {level.sku for location in LOCATIONS for level in inventory.levels_at(location)}
+    transfers = []
+    shortfalls = []
+    for sku in sorted(skus & set(rules)):
+        sku_transfers, sku_shortfalls = plan_sku(inventory, rules[sku])
+        transfers.extend(sku_transfers)
+        shortfalls.extend((sku, location, missing) for location, missing in sku_shortfalls)
+    return transfers, shortfalls
+
+
+def write_transfers_csv(path: str, transfers: list[Transfer]) -> None:
+    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.writer(handle)
+        writer.writerow(["sku", "source", "destination", "quantity"])
+        for transfer in transfers:
+            writer.writerow(
+                [transfer.sku, transfer.source, transfer.destination, transfer.quantity]
+            )
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(levelname)s: %(message)s")
+    if len(argv) != 3:
+        logger.error("usage: python -m stockroom.transfers LEVELS_CSV RULES_CSV OUTPUT_CSV")
+        return 2
+    levels_path, rules_path, output_path = argv
+    try:
+        levels = load_levels_csv(levels_path)
+        rules = load_rules_csv(rules_path)
+    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
+        logger.error("input file not found: %s", exc.filename)
+        return 2
+    levels = [level for level in levels if level.location in LOCATIONS]
+    transfers, shortfalls = plan_transfers(Inventory(levels), rules)
+    for sku, location, missing in shortfalls:
+        logger.warning("%s at %s is still short by %d units", sku, location, missing)
+    write_transfers_csv(output_path, transfers)
+    logger.info("%d transfers proposed", len(transfers))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

- Proposed transfers are `Transfer` records (`sku`, `source`, `destination`, `quantity`). The code that finds them is separate from the CSV writing, so other code can use the plan directly.

**Conventions**
`models.py` uses dataclasses, and `inventory.py`, `reorder.py` and `loader.py` use snake_case names and `logging`. The new code follows CLAUDE.md instead: `NamedTuple` records, camelCase names, `print()` for messages, and a single `unittest.TestCase` class. I left the existing modules unchanged. +"""Propose stock transfers between the main and shop locations.
+
+Usage: python -m stockroom.transfers LEVELS_CSV RULES_CSV OUTPUT_CSV
+"""
+import csv
+import os
+import sys
+from typing import NamedTuple
+
+from stockroom.inventory import Inventory
+from stockroom.loader import load_levels_csv, load_rules_csv
+from stockroom.models import ReorderRule
+from stockroom.reorder import needs_reorder
+
+LOCATIONS = ("main", "shop")
+
+
+class Transfer(NamedTuple):
+    sku: str
+    source: str
+    destination: str
+    quantity: int
+
+
+class Shortfall(NamedTuple):
+    sku: str
+    location: str
+    missing: int
+
+
+def targetLevel(rule: ReorderRule) -> int:
+    """Available stock a location should reach: one above the reorder point."""
+    return rule.reorder_point + 1
+
+
+def otherLocation(location: str) -> str:
+    return LOCATIONS[1] if location == LOCATIONS[0] else LOCATIONS[0]
+
+
+def planSku(
+    inventory: Inventory, sku: str, rule: ReorderRule
+) -> tuple[list[Transfer], list[Shortfall]]:
+    """Plan the transfers for one SKU and list the shortages left uncovered."""
+    transfers = []
+    shortfalls = []
+    target = targetLevel(rule)
+    for destination in LOCATIONS:
+        level = inventory.get_level(sku, destination)
+        if not needs_reorder(level, rule):
+            continue
+        source = otherLocation(destination)
+        sourceLevel = inventory.get_level(sku, source)
+        needed = target - level.available
+        spare = 0 if needs_reorder(sourceLevel, rule) else sourceLevel.available - target
+        quantity = min(needed, spare)
+        if quantity > 0:
+            transfers.append(Transfer(sku, source, destination, quantity))
+        if needed > quantity:
+            shortfalls.append(Shortfall(sku, destination, needed - max(quantity, 0)))
+    return transfers, shortfalls
+
+
+def planTransfers(
+    inventory: Inventory, rules: dict[str, ReorderRule]
+) -> tuple[list[Transfer], list[Shortfall]]:
+    """Plan transfers for every ruled SKU stocked at main or shop, in SKU order."""
+    skus = {level.sku for location in LOCATIONS for level in inventory.levels_at(location)}
+    transfers = []
+    shortfalls = []
+    for sku in sorted(skus & rules.keys()):
+        skuTransfers, skuShortfalls = planSku(inventory, sku, rules[sku])
+        transfers.extend(skuTransfers)
+        shortfalls.extend(skuShortfalls)
+    return transfers, shortfalls
+
+
+def writeTransfers(path: str, transfers: list[Transfer]) -> None:
+    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.writer(handle)
+        writer.writerow(Transfer._fields)
+        writer.writerows(transfers)
+
+
+def reportShortfalls(shortfalls: list[Shortfall]) -> None:
+    for shortfall in shortfalls:
+        print(
+            f"warning: {shortfall.sku} is short at {shortfall.location}: "
+            f"{shortfall.missing} units still missing",
+            file=sys.stderr,
+        )
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    args = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
+    if len(args) != 3:
+        print("usage: python -m stockroom.transfers LEVELS_CSV RULES_CSV OUTPUT_CSV",
+              file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    levelsPath, rulesPath, outputPath = args
+    for path in (levelsPath, rulesPath):
+        if not os.path.isfile(path):
+            print(f"error: file not found: {path}", file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+    levels = [level for level in load_levels_csv(levelsPath) if level.location in LOCATIONS]
+    transfers, shortfalls = planTransfers(Inventory(levels), load_rules_csv(rulesPath))
+    writeTransfers(outputPath, transfers)
+    reportShortfalls(shortfalls)
+    print(f"{len(transfers)} transfers proposed")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Budget alerts per category for one month.
+
+Usage: python -m budgetbook.alerts LEDGER BUDGETS MONTH OUTPUT [--near PERCENT]
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from enum import Enum
+from typing import Optional
+
+from budgetbook.budgets import loadBudgets
+from budgetbook.ledger import inMonth, loadTransactions
+from budgetbook.report import isMonth
+from budgetbook.summary import spentByCategory
+
+PERCENT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9]+")
+
+
+class AlertLevel(Enum):
+    OK = "ok"
+    NEAR = "near"
+    OVER = "over"
+
+
+def to_cents(amount) -> int:
+    """Convert a two-place amount from the readers to an integer number of cents."""
+    return int(amount.scaleb(2))
+
+
+def format_cents(cents: int) -> str:
+    """Format cents with two digits after the point, for example -510 as "-5.10"."""
+    sign = "-" if cents < 0 else ""
+    whole, fraction = divmod(abs(cents), 100)
+    return f"{sign}{whole}.{fraction:02d}"
+
+
+def alert_level(spent_cents: int, budget_cents: int, near_percent: Optional[int]) -> AlertLevel:
+    """Classify spending against a budget; no near threshold means never "near"."""
+    if spent_cents > budget_cents:
+        return AlertLevel.OVER
+    if near_percent is not None and spent_cents * 100 >= near_percent * budget_cents:
+        return AlertLevel.NEAR
+    return AlertLevel.OK
+
+
+def build_alerts(spent: dict, budgets: dict, near_percent: Optional[int]) -> list:
+    """One entry per budget category, sorted by category name."""
+    entries = []
+    for category in sorted(budgets):
+        budget_cents = to_cents(budgets[category])
+        spent_cents = to_cents(spent[category]) if category in spent else 0
+        entries.append({
+            "category": category,
+            "budget": format_cents(budget_cents),
+            "spent": format_cents(spent_cents),
+            "remaining": format_cents(budget_cents - spent_cents),
+            "level": alert_level(spent_cents, budget_cents, near_percent).value,
+        })
+    return entries
+
+
+def parse_percent(text: str) -> int:
+    """Parse a whole number from 1 to 100; raise ValueError otherwise."""
+    if PERCENT_PATTERN.fullmatch(text) is None or not 1 <= int(text) <= 100:
+        raise ValueError(f"percent must be a whole number from 1 to 100, got {text!r}")
+    return int(text)
+
+
+def parse_args(argv: Optional[list]) -> argparse.Namespace:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m budgetbook.alerts",
+                                     description="Write budget alert levels per category for one month.")
+    parser.add_argument("ledger", help="ledger CSV file")
+    parser.add_argument("budgets", help="budget CSV file (category,limit)")
+    parser.add_argument("month", help="month as YYYY-MM")
+    parser.add_argument("output", help="JSON file to write")
+    parser.add_argument("--near", help="percentage of the budget from which a category is near")
+    return parser.parse_args(argv)
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[list] = None) -> int:
+    args = parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        if not isMonth(args.month):
+            raise ValueError(f"month must look like 2024-03, got {args.month!r}")
+        near_percent = parse_percent(args.near) if args.near is not None else None
+        transactions = loadTransactions(args.ledger)
+        budgets = loadBudgets(args.budgets)
+        spent = spentByCategory(inMonth(transactions, args.month))
+        result = {
+            "month": args.month,
+            "near": near_percent,
+            "categories": build_alerts(spent, budgets, near_percent),
+        }
+        with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+            json.dump(result, fh, indent=2)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as err:
+        print(f"error: {err}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Expense claims: ``python -m payrun.expenses REGISTRY CLAIMS OUTPUT``.
+
+CLAIMS has one ``employee id,category,amount`` line per claim. OUTPUT is a JSON file with the
+amounts paid per employee, their total and the rejected claims.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from .employees import Employee, readRegistry
+
+CAP_CENTS: dict[str, int | None] = {
+    "travel": 50000,
+    "meals": 6000,
+    "equipment": None,
+}
+
+AMOUNT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"([0-9]+)(?:\.([0-9]{1,2}))?")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Claim:
+    """An approved claim: who gets paid, for what, and how much."""
+
+    employee: Employee
+    category: str
+    paid_cents: int
+
+
+def parse_claim_amount(text: str) -> tuple[int | None, str | None]:
+    """Parse a positive amount with at most two decimals into cents."""
+    match = AMOUNT_PATTERN.fullmatch(text)
+    if match is None:
+        return None, "amount is not a number with at most two decimals"
+    whole, fraction = match.groups()
+    amount_cents = int(whole) * 100 + int((fraction or "").ljust(2, "0"))
+    if amount_cents <= 0:
+        return None, "amount must be positive"
+    return amount_cents, None
+
+
+def check_claim(
+    line: str, registry: dict[str, Employee]
+) -> tuple[Claim | None, str | None]:
+    """Check one claim line against the registry; return ``(claim, None)`` or ``(None, reason)``."""
+    parts = [part.strip() for part in line.split(",")]
+    if len(parts) != 3:
+        return None, f"expected 3 fields, got {len(parts)}"
+    employee_id, category, amount_text = parts
+    if category not in CAP_CENTS:
+        return None, f"unknown category {category!r}"
+    amount_cents, error = parse_claim_amount(amount_text)
+    if error is not None:
+        return None, error
+    employee = registry.get(employee_id)
+    if employee is None:
+        return None, f"unknown employee {employee_id!r}"
+    cap_cents = CAP_CENTS[category]
+    paid_cents = amount_cents if cap_cents is None else min(amount_cents, cap_cents)
+    return Claim(employee, category, paid_cents), None
+
+
+def format_cents(cents: int) -> str:
+    """Format cents as a plain amount with two decimals."""
+    return f"{cents // 100}.{cents % 100:02d}"
+
+
+def process_claims(lines: list[str], registry: dict[str, Employee]) -> dict:
+    """Build the output report from the claim lines."""
+    paid_cents: dict[str, int] = {}
+    rejected = []
+    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
+        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        claim, error = check_claim(line, registry)
+        if error is not None:
+            rejected.append({"line": number, "reason": error})
+            continue
+        employee_id = claim.employee.employeeId
+        paid_cents[employee_id] = paid_cents.get(employee_id, 0) + claim.paid_cents
+    return {
+        "paid": {key: format_cents(value) for key, value in paid_cents.items()},
+        "total": format_cents(sum(paid_cents.values())),
+        "rejected": rejected,
+    }
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Process the expense claims and return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="payrun.expenses", description="Pay expense claims.")
+    parser.add_argument("registry", help="employee registry file")
+    parser.add_argument("claims", help="claims, one 'employee id,category,amount' line each")
+    parser.add_argument("output", help="JSON file to write the report to")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        registry = readRegistry(args.registry)
+        with open(args.claims, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            lines = handle.read().splitlines()
+    except (OSError, ValueError, ArithmeticError) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc.args[0] if exc.args else exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    report = process_claims(lines, registry)
+    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        json.dump(report, handle, indent=2)
+        handle.write("\n")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Expense claims: ``python -m payrun.expenses REGISTRY CLAIMS OUTPUT``.

+amount paid per employee, the total paid and the rejected claims.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, localcontext
+
+from payrun.employees import Employee, readRegistry
+
+# Cap per claim (None means paid in full); a category that is not listed is not accepted.
+CLAIM_CAPS: dict[str, Decimal | None] = {
+    "travel": Decimal("500.00"),
+    "meals": Decimal("60.00"),
+    "equipment": None,
+}
+
+AMOUNT_PATTERN = re.compile(r"[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,2})?", re.ASCII)
+
+
+def checkClaim(registry: dict[str, Employee], line: str) -> tuple[Employee, str, Decimal]:
+    """Check one claim line; return the employee, the category and the amount to pay.
+
+    Raises ``ValueError`` with a short reason when the claim is rejected.
+    """
+    parts = [p.strip() for p in line.split(",")]
+    if len(parts) != 3:
+        raise ValueError(f"expected 3 fields, got {len(parts)}")
+    employeeId, category, amountText = parts
+    if not AMOUNT_PATTERN.fullmatch(amountText):
+        raise ValueError(f"invalid amount {amountText!r}")
+    amount = Decimal(amountText)
+    if amount <= 0:
+        raise ValueError(f"amount must be positive: {amountText!r}")
+    if category not in CLAIM_CAPS:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown category {category!r}")
+    if employeeId not in registry:
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown employee {employeeId!r}")
+    cap = CLAIM_CAPS[category]
+    if cap is not None and amount > cap:
+        amount = cap
+    return registry[employeeId], category, amount
+
+
+def exactSum(values: list[Decimal]) -> Decimal:
+    """Add amounts without losing digits, whatever their size."""
+    with localcontext() as context:
+        context.prec = 10 + sum(len(v.as_tuple().digits) for v in values)
+        return sum(values, Decimal("0.00"))
+
+
+def processClaims(registry: dict[str, Employee], lines: list[str]) -> dict:
+    """Process the claim lines and build the report written to OUTPUT."""
+    amounts: dict[str, list[Decimal]] = {}
+    rejected = []
+    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
+        if not line.strip() or line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        try:
+            employee, _category, amount = checkClaim(registry, line)
+        except ValueError as exc:
+            rejected.append({"line": number, "reason": str(exc)})
+            continue
+        amounts.setdefault(employee.employeeId, []).append(amount)
+    totals = {employeeId: exactSum(values) for employeeId, values in amounts.items()}
+    return {
+        "paid": {employeeId: f"{total:.2f}" for employeeId, total in totals.items()},
+        "total": f"{exactSum(list(totals.values())):.2f}",
+        "rejected": rejected,
+    }
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Process the expense claims and return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="payrun.expenses", description="Pay expense claims.")
+    parser.add_argument("registry", help="employee registry file")
+    parser.add_argument("claims", help="claims, one 'employee id,category,amount' line each")
+    parser.add_argument("output", help="JSON file to write the report to")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        registry = readRegistry(args.registry)
+        with open(args.claims, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            lines = handle.read().splitlines()
+    except (OSError, ValueError, InvalidOperation) as exc:
+        print(f"error: {exc.args[0] if exc.args else exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    report = processClaims(registry, lines)
+    with open(args.output, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        json.dump(report, handle, indent=2)
+        handle.write("\n")
+    return 0
+
+

+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="couponkit.stack")

+    limit = round_amount(subtotal * max_percent / 100)
+    discount = ZERO

+    applied = []
+    rejected = []

+"""Write a shopping list for a meal plan: python -m recipebox.shopping PLAN OUTPUT."""
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import sys
+from typing import Dict, List, NamedTuple, Optional, Tuple
+
+from recipebox.models import Ingredient
+from recipebox.parser import load_recipe
+from recipebox.scaling import format_ingredient, round_quantity, scale_recipe
+from recipebox.units import to_base_unit
+
+
+class PlanEntry(NamedTuple):
+    """One plan line: a recipe file name and the servings to cook."""
+
+    fileName: str
+    servings: int
+
+
+class ShoppingItem(NamedTuple):
+    """One thing to buy: a total in a base unit and the recipes that use it."""
+
+    name: str
+    quantity: float
+    unit: str
+    recipes: List[str]
+
+
+def parsePlan(text: str) -> List[PlanEntry]:
+    """Parse plan text into entries, raising ValueError on a bad line."""
+    entries: List[PlanEntry] = []
+    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
+        if not line.strip():
+            continue
+        parts = line.split()
+        if len(parts) < 2:
+            raise ValueError(f"line {number}: expected a recipe file name and servings")
+        servings = parts[-1]
+        if not (servings.isascii() and servings.isdigit()) or int(servings) < 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"line {number}: servings must be a whole number of at least 1, got {servings!r}"
+            )
+        fileName = line.strip().rsplit(None, 1)[0]
+        entries.append(PlanEntry(fileName, int(servings)))
+    return entries
+
+
+def buildShoppingList(planPath: str) -> List[ShoppingItem]:
+    """Read a plan and its recipes and return the combined shopping items."""
+    with open(planPath, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        entries = parsePlan(handle.read())
+    folder = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(planPath))
+    totals: Dict[Tuple[str, str], float] = {}
+    titles: Dict[Tuple[str, str], List[str]] = {}
+    for entry in entries:
+        recipePath = os.path.join(folder, entry.fileName)
+        try:
+            recipe = load_recipe(recipePath)
+            scaled = scale_recipe(recipe, entry.servings)
+        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+            raise ValueError(f"{entry.fileName}: {error}") from error
+        for ingredient in scaled.ingredients:
+            quantity, unit = to_base_unit(ingredient.quantity, ingredient.unit)
+            key = (ingredient.name.lower(), unit)
+            totals[key] = totals.get(key, 0.0) + quantity
+            used = titles.setdefault(key, [])
+            if scaled.title not in used:
+                used.append(scaled.title)
+    return [
+        ShoppingItem(name, round_quantity(totals[(name, unit)]), unit, titles[(name, unit)])
+        for name, unit in sorted(totals)
+    ]
+
+
+def formatItem(item: ShoppingItem) -> str:
+    """Return a shopping line such as "650 g flour (Pancakes, Bread)"."""
+    amount = format_ingredient(Ingredient(item.name, item.quantity, item.unit))
+    return f"{amount} ({', '.join(item.recipes)})"
+
+
+def writeShoppingList(items: List[ShoppingItem], outputPath: str) -> None:
+    """Write the shopping items as JSON with "items" and "lines"."""
+    data = {
+        "items": [
+            {"name": item.name, "quantity": item.quantity, "unit": item.unit, "recipes": item.recipes}
+            for item in items
+        ],
+        "lines": [formatItem(item) for item in items],
+    }
+    with open(outputPath, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        json.dump(data, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
+        handle.write("\n")
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
+    """Run the command and return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        prog="python -m recipebox.shopping", description="Write a shopping list for a meal plan."
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("plan", metavar="PLAN", help="plan file: lines of 'recipe-file servings'")
+    parser.add_argument("output", metavar="OUTPUT", help="JSON file to write")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        items = buildShoppingList(args.plan)
+        writeShoppingList(items, args.output)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Shopping list for a meal plan: python -m recipebox.shopping PLAN OUTPUT."""

+import os

+

+from recipebox.parser import load_recipe
+from recipebox.scaling import format_ingredient, round_quantity, scale_recipe
+from recipebox.units import to_base_unit
+
+_SERVINGS_RE = re.compile(r"^[0-9]+$")
+
+
+def parse_plan(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, int]]:
+    """Parse plan text into (recipe file name, servings) pairs."""
+    entries = []
+    for number, line in enumerate(text.splitlines(), start=1):
+        if not line.strip():
+            continue
+        words = line.split()
+        if len(words) != 2:
+            raise ValueError("plan line {}: expected a recipe file and servings, got {!r}".format(number, line))
+        file_name, servings_text = words
+        if _SERVINGS_RE.match(servings_text) is None or int(servings_text) < 1:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "plan line {}: servings must be a whole number of at least 1, got {!r}".format(number, servings_text)
+            )
+        entries.append((file_name, int(servings_text)))
+    return entries
+
+
+def build_shopping_list(plan_path: str) -> dict:
+    """Read a plan and return the shopping list with "items" and "lines"."""
+    with open(plan_path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        entries = parse_plan(handle.read())
+    folder = os.path.dirname(plan_path)
+    totals: dict[tuple[str, str], float] = {}
+    titles: dict[tuple[str, str], list[str]] = {}
+    for file_name, servings in entries:
+        recipe = load_recipe(os.path.join(folder, file_name))
+        if recipe.servings < 1:
+            raise ValueError("{}: recipe must serve at least 1".format(file_name))
+        for item in scale_recipe(recipe, servings).ingredients:
+            quantity, unit = to_base_unit(item.quantity, item.unit)
+            key = (item.name.lower(), unit)
+            totals[key] = totals.get(key, 0.0) + quantity
+            if recipe.title not in titles.setdefault(key, []):
+                titles[key].append(recipe.title)
+    items = []
+    lines = []
+    for key in sorted(totals):
+        name, unit = key
+        quantity = round_quantity(totals[key])
+        items.append({"name": name, "quantity": quantity, "unit": unit, "recipes": titles[key]})
+        amount = format_ingredient(Ingredient(name, quantity, unit))
+        lines.append("{} ({})".format(amount, ", ".join(titles[key])))
+    return {"items": items, "lines": lines}
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    """Run the command and return the exit status."""
+    if len(argv) != 2:
+        print("usage: python -m recipebox.shopping PLAN OUTPUT", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    plan_path, output_path = argv
+    try:
+        result = build_shopping_list(plan_path)
+        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(result, handle, indent=2)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+        print("error: {}".format(error), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+"""Promo codes: what a code would take off a cart. Run as python -m cartkit.promo."""
+import csv
+import io
+import json
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+
+from cartkit.cart import Cart
+from cartkit.catalog import load_catalog
+from cartkit.errors import (
+    CartError,
+    InvalidPriceError,
+    InvalidPromoError,
+    InvalidQuantityError,
+    MinimumSpendError,
+    UnknownPromoCodeError,
+)
+from cartkit.money import format_price, parse_price, percent_of
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PromoCode:
+    """One promo code; value is a whole percent or an amount in cents."""
+
+    code: str
+    kind: str
+    value: int
+    min_spend_cents: int
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class PromoResult:
+    """The effect of a promo code on a cart, in cents."""
+
+    code: str
+    subtotal_cents: int
+    discount_cents: int
+
+    @property
+    def total_cents(self) -> int:
+        """Return the subtotal minus the discount."""
+        return self.subtotal_cents - self.discount_cents
+
+
+def load_promo_codes(csv_text: str) -> list[PromoCode]:
+    """Build promo codes from CSV text with columns code,kind,value,min_spend."""
+    codes = []
+    reader = csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(csv_text))
+    for row_number, row in enumerate(reader, start=2):
+        try:
+            codes.append(_parse_code_row(row))
+        except (InvalidPriceError, ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, AttributeError):
+            raise InvalidPromoError("row {}: invalid promo code row".format(row_number)) from None
+    return codes
+
+
+def _parse_code_row(row: dict) -> PromoCode:
+    kind = row["kind"].strip()
+    value_text = row["value"].strip()
+    if kind == "percent":
+        if not value_text.isdigit() or not 1 <= int(value_text) <= 100:
+            raise ValueError("percent must be a whole number from 1 to 100")
+        value = int(value_text)
+    elif kind == "fixed":
+        value = parse_price(value_text)
+    else:
+        raise ValueError("unknown kind")
+    min_spend_text = row["min_spend"].strip()
+    min_spend_cents = parse_price(min_spend_text) if min_spend_text else 0
+    return PromoCode(row["code"].strip(), kind, value, min_spend_cents)
+
+
+def apply_promo(cart: Cart, codes: list[PromoCode], typed: str) -> PromoResult:
+    """Return what the code typed by the customer takes off the cart."""
+    wanted = typed.strip().casefold()
+    for promo in codes:
+        if promo.code.casefold() == wanted:
+            break
+    else:
+        raise UnknownPromoCodeError("unknown promo code: {}".format(typed))
+    subtotal = cart.subtotal()
+    if subtotal < promo.min_spend_cents:
+        raise MinimumSpendError(
+            "promo code {} needs a subtotal of at least {}, cart has {}".format(
+                promo.code, format_price(promo.min_spend_cents), format_price(subtotal)
+            )
+        )
+    if promo.kind == "percent":
+        discount = percent_of(subtotal, promo.value * 100)
+    else:
+        discount = promo.value
+    return PromoResult(promo.code, subtotal, min(discount, subtotal))
+
+
+def load_order(catalog_text: str, order_text: str) -> Cart:
+    """Build a cart from order CSV text with columns sku,quantity."""
+    cart = Cart(load_catalog(catalog_text))
+    for row_number, row in enumerate(csv.DictReader(io.StringIO(order_text)), start=2):
+        try:
+            quantity = int(row["quantity"])
+        except (ValueError, TypeError):
+            raise InvalidQuantityError("row {}: invalid quantity".format(row_number)) from None
+        cart.add(row["sku"].strip(), quantity)
+    return cart
+
+
+def result_to_json(result: PromoResult) -> dict:
+    """Return the output document for a promo result."""
+    discount = format_price(result.discount_cents)
+    return {
+        "code": result.code,
+        "subtotal": format_price(result.subtotal_cents)[1:],
+        "discount": discount[1:],
+        "total": format_price(result.total_cents)[1:],
+        "line": "Promo {}: -{}".format(result.code, discount),
+    }
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    """Run the command and return the exit status."""
+    if len(argv) != 5:
+        print("usage: python -m cartkit.promo CATALOG ORDER CODES CODE OUTPUT", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    catalog_path, order_path, codes_path, typed, output_path = argv
+    try:
+        texts = []
+        for path in (catalog_path, order_path, codes_path):
+            with open(path, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as handle:
+                texts.append(handle.read())
+        cart = load_order(texts[0], texts[1])
+        result = apply_promo(cart, load_promo_codes(texts[2]), typed)
+        with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+            json.dump(result_to_json(result), handle, indent=2)
+    except (CartError, OSError) as exc:
+        print("error: {}".format(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

+"""Late fees: work out the status and fee of every tenant at a cut-off date.
+
+Usage: python -m rentroll.latefees TENANTS LEDGER DATE OUTPUT
+"""
+import argparse
+import json
+import logging
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import date
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal
+
+from rentroll.errors import InvalidDateError, RentrollError, UnknownUnitError
+from rentroll.ledger import LedgerEntry, load_ledger, signed_amount
+from rentroll.tenants import Tenant, load_tenants
+
+CURRENT = "current"
+LATE = "late"
+DELINQUENT = "delinquent"
+
+LATE_FEE_RATE = Decimal("0.05")
+DELINQUENT_FEE_RATE = Decimal("0.10")
+CENT = Decimal("0.01")
+
+logger = logging.getLogger("rentroll")
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class LateFee:
+    """The late fee result of one tenant. balance and fee are in currency units."""
+
+    unit: str
+    tenant: str
+    balance: Decimal
+    status: str
+    fee: Decimal
+
+
+def round_money(amount: Decimal) -> Decimal:
+    """Round an amount to two digits after the point, halves up."""
+    return amount.quantize(CENT, rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
+
+
+def format_money(amount: Decimal) -> str:
+    """Format an amount with two digits after the point, for example "-40.00"."""
+    return str(round_money(amount))
+
+
+def parse_cutoff(text: str) -> date:
+    """Parse a YYYY-MM-DD date; raise InvalidDateError if it is not one."""
+    try:
+        day = date.fromisoformat(text)
+    except ValueError:
+        raise InvalidDateError(text) from None
+    if day.isoformat() != text:
+        raise InvalidDateError(text)
+    return day
+
+
+def status_and_fee(balance: Decimal, rent: Decimal) -> tuple[str, Decimal]:
+    """Return the status and the rounded fee for a balance and a monthly rent."""
+    if balance <= 0:
+        return CURRENT, round_money(Decimal(0))
+    if balance <= rent:
+        return LATE, round_money(rent * LATE_FEE_RATE)
+    return DELINQUENT, round_money(balance * DELINQUENT_FEE_RATE)
+
+
+def late_fees(tenants: list[Tenant], entries: list[LedgerEntry], cutoff: date) -> list[LateFee]:
+    """Return one LateFee per tenant, in the order of tenants.
+
+    Only entries dated on or before cutoff count. Raises UnknownUnitError if any
+    entry names a unit without a tenant.
+    """
+    cents: dict[str, int] = {tenant.unit: 0 for tenant in tenants}
+    for entry in entries:
+        if entry.unit not in cents:
+            raise UnknownUnitError(entry.unit)
+        if entry.day <= cutoff:
+            cents[entry.unit] += signed_amount(entry)
+    results = []
+    for tenant in tenants:
+        balance = Decimal(cents[tenant.unit]) / 100
+        status, fee = status_and_fee(balance, Decimal(tenant.rent) / 100)
+        results.append(LateFee(tenant.unit, tenant.name, round_money(balance), status, fee))
+    return results
+
+
+def write_late_fees(results: list[LateFee], cutoff_text: str, path: str) -> None:
+    """Write the late fee results as JSON."""
+    document = {
+        "date": cutoff_text,
+        "tenants": [
+            {
+                "unit": result.unit,
+                "tenant": result.tenant,
+                "balance": format_money(result.balance),
+                "status": result.status,
+                "fee": format_money(result.fee),
+            }
+            for result in results
+        ],
+        "total": format_money(sum((result.fee for result in results), Decimal(0))),
+    }
+    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        json.dump(document, handle, indent=2)
+        handle.write("\n")
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Run the late fee command. Return the exit status."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m rentroll.latefees")
+    parser.add_argument("tenants")
+    parser.add_argument("ledger")
+    parser.add_argument("date")
+    parser.add_argument("output")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        cutoff = parse_cutoff(args.date)
+        tenants = load_tenants(args.tenants)
+        entries = load_ledger(args.ledger)
+        results = late_fees(tenants, entries, cutoff)
+        write_late_fees(results, args.date, args.output)
+    except (RentrollError, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        logger.error(f"error: {exc}")
+        return 2
+    logger.info(f"wrote late fees of {len(results)} tenants to {args.output}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(message)s")
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Vacation plan: the days on which a neighbour has to water the plants while we are away."""
+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+from datetime import date, timedelta
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Optional
+
+from plantcare.plants import Plant, load_plants
+from plantcare.settings import load_settings
+
+
+def plant_visits(plant: Plant, leave: date, back: date, max_dry_days: int) -> list[date]:
+    """Return the days the neighbour waters ``plant``, earliest first."""
+    longest = timedelta(days=plant.interval + max_dry_days)
+    last = leave - timedelta(days=1)
+    visits = []
+    while back - last > longest:
+        last += longest
+        visits.append(last)
+    return visits
+
+
+def plan_visits(plants: list[Plant], leave: date, back: date, max_dry_days: int) -> dict:
+    """Return the vacation plan: the visits per plant and the plants to water per day."""
+    per_plant = [(plant, plant_visits(plant, leave, back, max_dry_days)) for plant in plants]
+    by_day: dict[date, list[str]] = {}
+    for plant, visits in per_plant:
+        for day in visits:
+            by_day.setdefault(day, []).append(plant.name)
+    return {
+        "plants": [{"name": plant.name, "visits": [day.isoformat() for day in visits]}
+                   for plant, visits in per_plant],
+        "days": [{"date": day.isoformat(), "plants": by_day[day]} for day in sorted(by_day)],
+    }
+
+
+def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    """Return the argument parser of the vacation command."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="plantcare.vacation")
+    parser.add_argument("leave", metavar="LEAVE", type=date.fromisoformat,
+                        help="the first day away, YYYY-MM-DD")
+    parser.add_argument("back", metavar="BACK", type=date.fromisoformat,
+                        help="the day we are home again, YYYY-MM-DD")
+    parser.add_argument("output", metavar="OUTPUT_FILE", type=Path, help="the plan file to write")
+    parser.add_argument("--settings", type=Path, help="settings file with key = value lines")
+    parser.add_argument("--max-dry", type=int, metavar="DAYS",
+                        help="days a plant may go without water past its interval")
+    return parser
+
+
+def main(argv: Optional[list[str]] = None) -> int:
+    """Run the vacation command and return the exit status."""
+    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        settings = load_settings(args.settings)
+        plants = load_plants(settings.plants_file, settings.default_interval)
+        max_dry = settings.max_dry_days if args.max_dry is None else args.max_dry
+        if max_dry < 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"max dry days must be 0 or more, not {max_dry}")
+        if args.back <= args.leave:
+            raise ValueError(f"BACK ({args.back}) must be after LEAVE ({args.leave})")
+        plan = plan_visits(plants, args.leave, args.back, max_dry)
+        args.output.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+        args.output.write_text(json.dumps(plan, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
+    except (OSError, ValueError, KeyError) as error:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    print(f"the neighbour has to come on {len(plan['days'])} days")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Compare two price lists and report the products whose price changed a lot."""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import sys
+from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, InvalidOperation, localcontext
+
+from pricewatch.pricelist import PriceItem, loadPriceList
+
+DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = "10"
+HEADER = ("sku", "name", "old", "new", "change", "percent")
+
+
+def parse_threshold(text: str) -> tuple[Decimal | None, str | None]:
+    """Return ``(threshold, None)`` for a number above zero, else ``(None, error)``."""
+    try:
+        value = Decimal(text.strip())
+    except InvalidOperation:
+        return None, f"bad threshold: {text}"
+    if not value.is_finite():
+        return None, f"bad threshold: {text}"
+    if value <= 0:
+        return None, f"threshold must be above zero: {text}"
+    return value, None
+
+
+def read_price_list(path: str) -> tuple[dict[str, PriceItem] | None, str | None]:
+    """Return ``(items, None)`` for a readable price list, else ``(None, error)``."""
+    try:
+        return loadPriceList(path), None
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+        return None, f"{path}: {error}"
+
+
+def compare_lists(
+    old: dict[str, PriceItem], new: dict[str, PriceItem], threshold: Decimal
+) -> list[list[str]]:
+    """Return the output rows, sorted by sku, of the products that changed by the threshold."""
+    cent = Decimal("0.01")
+    rows = []
+    for sku in sorted(old.keys() & new.keys()):
+        old_price = Decimal(old[sku].price) * cent
+        new_price = Decimal(new[sku].price) * cent
+        change = new_price - old_price
+        with localcontext() as context:
+            context.prec = 50
+            if abs(change) * 100 < threshold * old_price:
+                continue
+            percent = (change * 100 / old_price).quantize(Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
+        rows.append([
+            sku,
+            new[sku].name,
+            f"{old_price.quantize(cent)}",
+            f"{new_price.quantize(cent)}",
+            f"{change.quantize(cent):+}",
+            f"{percent:+}",
+        ])
+    return rows
+
+
+def write_report(path: str, rows: list[list[str]]) -> None:
+    """Write the header row and ``rows`` to ``path`` as CSV."""
+    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.writer(handle)
+        writer.writerow(HEADER)
+        writer.writerows(rows)
+
+
+def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    """Return the argument parser of the compare command."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pricewatch.compare")
+    parser.add_argument("old_file", help="old price list CSV file")
+    parser.add_argument("new_file", help="new price list CSV file")
+    parser.add_argument("output_file", help="CSV file to write")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--threshold",
+        default=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
+        help="smallest percent change to report, above zero (default 10)",
+    )
+    return parser
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Run the compare command and return the exit status."""
+    args = build_parser().parse_args(argv)
+    threshold, error = parse_threshold(args.threshold)
+    if error:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    old, error = read_price_list(args.old_file)
+    if error:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    new, error = read_price_list(args.new_file)
+    if error:
+        print(f"error: {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    rows = compare_lists(old, new, threshold)
+    try:
+        write_report(args.output_file, rows)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        print(f"error: {args.output_file}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+"""Compare two price lists and report the products whose price changed a lot."""
+import argparse
+import csv
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from decimal import Decimal, InvalidOperation, ROUND_HALF_UP
+
+from pricewatch.money import formatCents
+from pricewatch.pricelist import PriceItem, loadPriceList
+
+COLUMNS = ("sku", "name", "old", "new", "change", "percent")
+DEFAULT_THRESHOLD = "10"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PriceChange:
+    """A product present in both lists. Prices and ``change`` are in cents."""
+
+    sku: str
+    name: str
+    old: int
+    new: int
+
+    @property
+    def change(self) -> int:
+        return self.new - self.old
+
+
+def parseThreshold(text: str) -> Decimal:
+    """Return the threshold in ``text`` as a number above zero."""
+    try:
+        value = Decimal(text.strip())
+    except InvalidOperation:
+        raise ValueError("threshold is not a number: {!r}".format(text)) from None
+    if not value.is_finite():
+        raise ValueError("threshold is not a number: {!r}".format(text))
+    if value <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("threshold must be above zero, not {}".format(text))
+    return value
+
+
+def bigChanges(old: dict[str, PriceItem], new: dict[str, PriceItem],
+               threshold: Decimal) -> list[PriceChange]:
+    """Return the changes of skus in both lists that reach ``threshold`` percent, by sku."""
+    changes = []
+    for sku in sorted(old.keys() & new.keys()):
+        change = PriceChange(sku, new[sku].name, old[sku].price, new[sku].price)
+        # abs(change) / old * 100 >= threshold, without any rounding
+        if abs(change.change) * 100 >= threshold * change.old:
+            changes.append(change)
+    return changes
+
+
+def formatSigned(text: str, negative: bool) -> str:
+    """Put a sign in front of an unsigned number text."""
+    return ("-" if negative else "+") + text
+
+
+def formatRow(change: PriceChange) -> list[str]:
+    """Return the CSV fields of ``change``."""
+    negative = change.change < 0
+    percent = (abs(Decimal(change.change) * 100) / Decimal(change.old)).quantize(
+        Decimal("0.1"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
+    return [
+        change.sku,
+        change.name,
+        formatCents(change.old),
+        formatCents(change.new),
+        formatSigned(formatCents(abs(change.change)), negative),
+        formatSigned(str(percent), negative),
+    ]
+
+
+def writeChanges(path: str, changes: list[PriceChange]) -> None:
+    """Write ``changes`` to ``path`` as CSV."""
+    with open(path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.writer(handle)
+        writer.writerow(COLUMNS)
+        for change in changes:
+            writer.writerow(formatRow(change))
+
+
+def buildParser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
+    """Return the argument parser of the compare command."""
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="pricewatch.compare")
+    parser.add_argument("old_file", help="the older price list CSV file")
+    parser.add_argument("new_file", help="the newer price list CSV file")
+    parser.add_argument("output_file", help="CSV file to write")
+    parser.add_argument("--threshold", default=DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
+                        help="smallest percent change to report (default 10)")
+    return parser
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Run the compare command and return the exit status."""
+    args = buildParser().parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        threshold = parseThreshold(args.threshold)
+    except ValueError as error:
+        print("error: {}".format(error), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    loaded = []
+    for path in (args.old_file, args.new_file):
+        try:
+            loaded.append(loadPriceList(path))
+        except (OSError, ValueError) as error:
+            print("error: {}: {}".format(path, error), file=sys.stderr)
+            return 2
+    changes = bigChanges(loaded[0], loaded[1], threshold)
+    try:
+        writeChanges(args.output_file, changes)
+    except OSError as error:
+        print("error: {}: {}".format(args.output_file, error), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())

+    """Work out the notices to send on ``day``.

+    if final_days < 1:

+    notices = []

+        if loan.status != LOAN_ACTIVE:

+        elif days_late >= 1:

+    """Write notices to a CSV file with the header ``member,name,barcode,due,notice,fine``.

+        writer.writerow(HEADER)

+"""
+import csv

+import shutil
+import sys
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import List, Optional, Set
+

+

+

+USAGE = "usage: python -m photosort.organize SOURCE DEST [--dry-run]"
+
+MOVED = "moved"
+PLANNED = "planned"
+SKIPPED = "skipped"
+
+
+@dataclass
+class PlanEntry:
+    """What happens with one photo.
+
+    target is the path inside DEST with "/" as separator, or None for a skipped photo;
+    status is one of "planned", "moved" and "skipped".

+    photo: PhotoFile
+    target: Optional[str]
+    status: str
+
+

+    """Plan the target of each photo, in the order of photos.
+
+    A photo is skipped when its name holds no date, when a file already exists at its
+    target in dest, or when an earlier photo has the same target. Every other entry
+    gets the status "planned".
+    """
+    plan: List[PlanEntry] = []
+    taken_targets: Set[str] = set()
+    for photo in photos:
+        if photo.taken is None:
+            logger.warning("skipped %s: no date in the file name", photo.relpath)
+            plan.append(PlanEntry(photo, None, SKIPPED))
+            continue
+        name = photo.relpath.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
+        target = "%04d/%02d/%s" % (photo.taken.year, photo.taken.month, name)
+        if os.path.exists(os.path.join(dest, *target.split("/"))):
+            logger.warning("skipped %s: %s already exists in the destination", photo.relpath, target)
+            plan.append(PlanEntry(photo, None, SKIPPED))
+        elif target in taken_targets:
+            logger.warning("skipped %s: an earlier photo has the target %s", photo.relpath, target)
+            plan.append(PlanEntry(photo, None, SKIPPED))
+        else:
+            taken_targets.add(target)
+            plan.append(PlanEntry(photo, target, PLANNED))
+    return plan
+
+
+def carry_out(plan: List[PlanEntry], dest: str) -> None:
+    """Move each planned photo to its target and mark its entry as moved."""
+    for entry in plan:
+        if entry.status != PLANNED:
+            continue
+        target_path = os.path.join(dest, *entry.target.split("/"))
+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target_path), exist_ok=True)
+        shutil.move(entry.photo.path, target_path)
+        entry.status = MOVED
+
+

+    """Write dest/plan.csv with one row per entry, sorted by source."""
+    os.makedirs(dest, exist_ok=True)
+    rows = sorted(plan, key=lambda entry: entry.photo.relpath)
+    with open(os.path.join(dest, "plan.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
+        writer = csv.writer(handle)
+        writer.writerow(PLAN_COLUMNS)
+        for entry in rows:
+            writer.writerow([entry.photo.relpath, entry.target or "", entry.status])
+
+
+def main(argv: List[str]) -> int:
+    """Run the organize command and return its exit status."""
+    args = [arg for arg in argv if arg != "--dry-run"]
+    dry_run = len(args) != len(argv)
+    if len(args) != 2:
+        logger.error(USAGE)
+        return 2
+    source, dest = args
+    if not os.path.isdir(source):

+        return 2

+    moved = sum(1 for entry in plan if entry.status == MOVED)

+
+

+    :param page: the page reached, never more than ``pages``
+    :param pages: number of pages of the book
+    :param last: day of the most recent journal entry for the book, or None
+    """

+    member: str
+    page: int
+    pages: int
+    last: date | None
+
+    def percent(self) -> str:
+        """Return the share of the book read in percent.
+
+        :returns: text with exactly one digit after the point, such as ``25.7``
+        """
+        tenths = (self.page * 2000 + self.pages) // (2 * self.pages)
+        return "{}.{}".format(tenths // 10, tenths % 10)

+    """Work out the progress of every member in one book.
+
+    :param club: the loaded club

+        page = min(max((entry.page for entry in own), default=0), pages)
+        last = max((entry.day for entry in own), default=None)

+                "{}/{}".format(item.page, item.pages),
+                item.percent(),
+                item.last.isoformat() if item.last else "",
+            ])
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
+    """Write the reading progress of all members in one book.
+
+    :param argv: command line arguments without the program name
+    :returns: the exit status
+    """

+    parser.add_argument("club_dir")
+    parser.add_argument("book_id")
+    parser.add_argument("output")
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        club = load_club(args.club_dir)
+    except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
+        print("error: {}".format(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    if args.book_id not in club.books:
+        print("error: unknown book id {!r}".format(args.book_id), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    records = book_progress(club, args.book_id)
+    try:
+        write_progress(args.output, records)
+    except OSError as exc:
+        print("error: {}".format(exc), file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+    finished = sum(1 for item in records if item.page == item.pages)
+    not_started = sum(1 for item in records if item.page == 0)
+    print("wrote the progress in {} to {}".format(args.book_id, args.output))
+    print("{} finished, {} not started".format(finished, not_started))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main())
